label: second input step (t=1) when first token is one of b,f,j,k,m,p,r,s,z,1,3
explanation: Fires only at step t=1, when the second original token is input, and only if the first original token is in the fixed set {b,f,j,k,m,p,r,s,z,1,3}. On the dev split each of these 11 first tokens fires on 100% of its t=1 steps, and the other 19 tokens never fire. The current input token, L, and later history do not matter. It never fires at t=0, at t>=2, on the delimiter, or during the copy phase. Activation is nearly constant (median 1.435, max 1.598) and depends mostly on which first token it is: first token m gives the top activations (~1.60), while 1 and p are among the lowest (~0.83-0.86 of max).

issues: None material. Test split: precision 1.000, recall 1.000, F1 1.000, mass recall 1.000, correlation 0.999. Running misses on the test split found 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.
Dev profile backs every structural claim. All activation falls at t=1. Activity is zero at t=0, at t>=2, on the delimiter and in the copy phase. Median 1.435, max 1.598.
The index-to-token mapping is correct: [1,5,9,10,12,15,17,18,25,27,29] = b,f,j,k,m,p,r,s,z,1,3.
The magnitude claims are consistent with the per-token mass shares. Among first tokens, m has the largest share (0.099), and 1 (0.085) and p (0.086) the smallest, with equal firing counts.
The label and predicate match: prev_tok at t=1 is the first original token.
